text.tspan: AutonomousTrust
— Behavior-Aware Zero Trust for

svg.text: DON26BZ03-NV059 · continuous, autonomous, edge-resident trust enforcement across the MTC-A/X kill chain —
no reachable central authority required on the per-access hot path.

text.tspan: OPERATIONAL CONCEPT
· MTC-A/X MARITIME KILL CHAIN IN A CONTESTED (DDIL) ENVIRONMENT

g.text: REACH-BACK · DoD PKI / ICAM / PDP — ASHORE, VIA TACTICAL SATCOM
MTC-A/X COHORT — quorum-vouched at a capped tier when SATCOM is denied

svg.text: Reach-back infra — off the hot path
Resident AT agent — every ringed node

text.tspan: Bump-in-the-wire gateway
Cohort trust boundary

svg.text: CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS · MTC-A/X KILL CHAIN

text.tspan: In a Maritime Targeting Cell-Afloat/Expeditionary (MTC-A/X) engagement
thread, ISR sensors, a track-fusion/targeting node, and a fires/effects
console are spread across ships and disadvantaged nodes on tactical
SATCOM.
ZTA authentication opens the door; AT decides what
happens inside
— a resident AT agent (or bump-in-the-wire gateway)
at each endpoint is its local policy decision/enforcement point.
A sensor's tracks reach the targeting node only while both endpoints hold
reputation above the required tier. A sensor that is authenticated and
certificate-valid but
captured or spoofed
— injecting an off-track
return — drifts outside its learned behavioral envelope, loses reputation,
and is
autonomously slashed and tier-gated out of the fires path
, in
real time, with signed evidence; a human-on-the-loop retains fires override.
When the SATCOM link to the PDP and DoD PKI drops,
the cohort keeps
operating
: the targeting node is vouched by quorum at a capped tier,
each admission signed, and the audit reconciles on reconnect — no step
in the loop waits on a reachable central authority.

svg.text: DoD ICAM (X.509/OCSP), paid once off the hot path.
TPM / secure element, measured boot — captured-asset defense.
